Sample wording: adapt it to your country's law and your own practice.
This lease is made on {col:leases.signed} between the landlord, represented by the managing agent, and {col:leases.tenant_name} (the tenant).
1. The property: unit {col:leases.unit} in property {col:leases.prop}, let for residential use only.
2. Term: from {col:leases.start} to {col:leases.end}. Renewal is by written agreement before the end date.
3. Rent: {col:leases.rent} paid {col:leases.freq}, due on day {col:leases.due_day} of the period. Rent paid after the grace period carries the late fee set out by the managing agent.
4. Deposit: {col:leases.deposit}, held as security and returned within the agreed days after move-out, less any lawful deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear.
5. Use and care: the tenant keeps the unit clean, reports repairs promptly, does not sublet without written consent and allows entry for inspection or repair after notice.
6. Rent review: at renewal the rent may change by up to the agreed yearly increase of {col:leases.escal}, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
7. Ending the lease: either party gives written notice as required by law. Keys, meter readings and an inspection report are exchanged at move-out.
Our records show an overdue balance of {col:tenants.overdue} on your account for unit {col:tenants.unit}. The oldest unpaid amount is {col:tenants.oldest} days late.
Please pay the full amount within 7 days of this notice, or contact us today to agree a payment plan. Late fees continue to apply as set out in your lease.
If you have already paid, please send us the payment reference so we can update your account. Thank you.
Your lease for unit {col:renewals.unit} ends on {col:renewals.end}. We would be glad to have you stay.
We offer to renew your lease until {col:renewals.new_end} at a rent of {col:renewals.proposed} per payment (currently {col:renewals.current}).
Please reply within 30 days to accept, or contact us to discuss. If we do not hear from you, we will start preparing the unit for new tenants.
This is to let you know that we need to enter unit {col:notices.unit} for an inspection or repair.
Planned date: {col:notices.deadline}. The visit will take place during normal working hours and we will keep it short.
If the date does not suit you, please reply so that we can agree another time. Thank you for your cooperation.
This is formal notice that the rent for unit {col:renewals.unit} will change when your current lease ends on {col:renewals.end}.
From the renewal the rent will be {col:renewals.proposed} per payment, compared with {col:renewals.current} today, a change of {col:renewals.change}.
The new rent reflects the market for similar homes in the area. Please contact us with any questions; we value having you as our tenant.
This agreement is made on {col:plans.agreed} between the managing agent and {col:plans.name} (the tenant).
The tenant owes {col:plans.total} in unpaid rent and agrees to pay it in {col:plans.inst} instalments of {col:plans.each}, the first due on {col:plans.first_due}, in addition to the regular rent.
If an instalment or a regular rent payment is missed, the full remaining balance becomes due at once and the usual late fees apply.
Nothing in this agreement changes the other terms of the lease.

This agreement is made on {today} between {set:company} (the manager, acting for the property owners) and {col:vendors.name} (the vendor).
1. Services: the vendor provides {col:vendors.trade} services to the buildings we manage, on written or message work orders that state the property, the unit and the priority.

2. Rates: labour at {col:vendors.rate} per hour and a call-out fee of {col:vendors.callout}. Materials are charged at cost with the receipt attached. Work above {set:approval_limit} needs written approval before it starts.
3. Response: emergencies are attended within {set:t_emergency} day, urgent jobs within {set:t_urgent} days and routine jobs within {set:t_routine} days of the work order.
4. Insurance: the vendor keeps public liability insurance in force at all times and sends the new certificate before the current one ends on {col:vendors.ins_expiry}.
5. Quality: work is guaranteed against defects. Poor workmanship is put right at no cost. We rate every job, and the vendor keeps an average rating of at least {set:min_rating}.
6. Conduct: the vendor's staff carry identification, respect tenants' homes, keep the keys safe, return them the same day and leave the work area clean.
7. Payment: the vendor sends one invoice per job quoting the job number. We pay approved invoices within 30 days.

1. Services: the manager lets and manages the owner's properties, collects rent, pays approved bills, keeps the owner's ledger, and sends a statement every month.

2. Management fee: the fee type is "{col:agreements.ftype}". The percent fee is {col:agreements.pct} of rent collected; a flat fee is {col:agreements.flat} per unit let; above {col:agreements.tbreak} of rent in a month a tiered fee of {col:agreements.tpct} applies. The monthly minimum is {col:agreements.minfee}.
3. Leasing fees: a new lease carries a fee of {col:agreements.leasing} of the yearly rent; a renewal carries a flat fee of {col:agreements.renew}.
4. VAT: VAT at {set:vat} is added to all fees and shown on each statement.

5. Spending limit: the manager may pay repairs and bills up to {col:agreements.limit} without the owner's approval. Larger bills wait for the owner's written or messaged approval, except in an emergency that puts people or the building at risk.
6. Reserve: the manager keeps a reserve of {set:res_months} months of rent in the client account for repairs, and tops it up from rent received.
7. Payouts: the net balance, after bills, fees and reserve, is paid to the owner each month with the statement.
8. Client account: all money received is kept in a client account apart from the manager's own money, and reconciled every month.
